research.title: Saving the game and difficulty settings
research.text: In Al-Qadim: The Genie's Curse, you can save your progress at any point by opening the Options menu and selecting Save Game, which supports up to nine saved games. The game also provides Easy, Normal, and Hard difficulty settings that scale monster aggression. Saved games are restored with Load Game from the opening menu or from Options during play, and a current game that was not saved is lost when you load.

research.title: Game controls
aliases: how do i open the menu
how do i use an item
how do i talk to people
research.text: In the original rule book's default mouse mode you move by holding the right mouse button so the hero walks toward the arrow cursor, and the left button is the action button for talking, attacking and opening things. Clicking the genie's lamp at the top of the screen opens the menu (Inventory, Ready Weapon, View Stats, Options), and the space bar fires a readied sling or shard. Keyboard play uses the arrow keys to move, Ctrl as the action button and Esc for the menu; a joystick's first button acts, its second fires, and Esc opens the menu.

research.title: Experience and levels
research.text: Per the original rule book, the hero earns experience for solving puzzles, achieving goals and killing monsters, and gains hit points automatically at each new level. Experience needed: level 2 at 2,000; level 3 at 4,000; level 4 at 8,000; level 5 at 16,000; level 6 at 32,000; level 7 at 64,000; level 8 at 125,000; level 9 at 250,000. The hero starts as a second-level corsair, and View Stats in the menu shows the current experience total.

research.title: Hit points and healing
research.text: In the original rule book, hit points are shown by the red health bar at the top of the screen; at zero the hero dies and you must start a new game or load a saved one. Health comes back by drinking a healing potion or visiting places where healing is available, and the maximum only goes up by gaining a level. View Stats in the menu shows the numeric maximum.

research.title: Gold and gems
aliases: how much is a gem worth
research.text: The original rule book names gold and gems as the two currencies, with one gem worth about ten gold pieces. Most merchants prefer gold, some accept gems and a few require them. Gold and gems mostly come from looting monster lairs and from being paid for completing tasks.

research.title: Potion and oil effects in the rule book
aliases: potion effects in the rule book
how much does a healing potion heal
how many hit points does a healing potion restore
research.text: The original rule book lists the Healing potion as restoring 4 to 10 hit points and the Extra Healing potion as restoring 6 to 27. A Giant Strength potion adds 8 damage to each blow for a few minutes, and the oils of elemental invulnerability (air, earth, fire, water) briefly make you immune to damage from that type of elemental. Potions are single-use and last for different real-time durations, and drinking a second one while another is active cancels the first; this guide's shop descriptions word some of these effects differently.

research.title: Unlocking new sword moves
aliases: how do i get new sword moves
how do i unlock new swings
research.text: According to the original rule book, the hero learns two additional sword swings as he gains experience levels and trains with the Weapons Master: the second also hits to the left and right, and the third is a 360-degree swing that also hits behind. When he becomes eligible you must guide him to the Weapons Master, who trains him quickly, and the next action circle lights up once the swing is available.

research.title: Ghoul
research.text: In the original rule book's bestiary the ghoul is an undead scavenger that often appears in packs, and its claws can paralyse a target for a short time. A person killed by ghouls becomes a ghoul unless the body is consumed.

sources.label: Al-Qadim: The Genie's Curse rule book (SSI, 1994), MOCAGH copy; wording checked 21 October 2026 against the same manual shipped with this guide (alqadim/al-qadim_manual_PDF.pdf)

research.title: Mummy
research.text: The original rule book describes mummies as powerful undead that rot whatever they kill. Their one major weakness is flame, so fire-based spells do them extra damage.

sources.label: Al-Qadim: The Genie's Curse rule book (SSI, 1994), MOCAGH copy; wording checked 21 October 2026 against the same manual shipped with this guide (alqadim/al-qadim_manual_PDF.pdf)

research.title: Huge spider
research.text: The original rule book describes huge spiders as aggressive, roughly six-foot predators of dungeons that usually come in groups and are hard to spot in shadow. Their poison is weaker in this game, so a bite does damage instead of killing outright.

sources.label: Al-Qadim: The Genie's Curse rule book (SSI, 1994), MOCAGH copy; wording checked 21 October 2026 against the same manual shipped with this guide (alqadim/al-qadim_manual_PDF.pdf)

research.title: Great ghul
research.text: Great ghuls are undead cousins of the genies that can change shape and turn invisible mid-fight, and they hit hard with claws and teeth. According to the original rule book, an invisible ghul can still damage you and be damaged.

sources.label: Al-Qadim: The Genie's Curse rule book (SSI, 1994), MOCAGH copy; wording checked 21 October 2026 against the same manual shipped with this guide (alqadim/al-qadim_manual_PDF.pdf)

research.title: Nas nas
research.text: The original rule book describes the nas nas as a hopping, one-armed, half-human creature made by evil wizards. It moves quickly and fights wildly with a scimitar.

sources.label: Al-Qadim: The Genie's Curse rule book (SSI, 1994), MOCAGH copy; wording checked 21 October 2026 against the same manual shipped with this guide (alqadim/al-qadim_manual_PDF.pdf)

research.title: Ogrima
research.text: The original rule book calls the ogrima a strong, cunning cross between an ogre and an ogre mage, about nine feet tall, with limited spellcasting and natural regeneration. It tends to avoid armor.

sources.label: Al-Qadim: The Genie's Curse rule book (SSI, 1994), MOCAGH copy; wording checked 21 October 2026 against the same manual shipped with this guide (alqadim/al-qadim_manual_PDF.pdf)

research.title: Debbi
research.text: According to the original rule book, debbis are two-foot desert scavengers, part baboon and part hyena, whose fear-causing ability sometimes throws magical sparks. They are cowards at heart, though locals report them growing bolder.

sources.label: Al-Qadim: The Genie's Curse rule book (SSI, 1994), MOCAGH copy; wording checked 21 October 2026 against the same manual shipped with this guide (alqadim/al-qadim_manual_PDF.pdf)

research.title: Werehyena
research.text: The original rule book describes the werehyena as a lycanthrope that changes between human and giant-hyena form. It usually fights as a six-foot hyena with massive jaws and is somewhat afraid of fire.

sources.label: Al-Qadim: The Genie's Curse rule book (SSI, 1994), MOCAGH copy; wording checked 21 October 2026 against the same manual shipped with this guide (alqadim/al-qadim_manual_PDF.pdf)

research.title: Ammut
research.text: The original rule book describes the ammut as a crocodile, hippopotamus and lioness cross that dislikes light and is usually found underground. It kills the honorable as well as the wicked and plays with the corpse.

sources.label: Al-Qadim: The Genie's Curse rule book (SSI, 1994), MOCAGH copy; wording checked 21 October 2026 against the same manual shipped with this guide (alqadim/al-qadim_manual_PDF.pdf)

research.title: Pirates
research.text: According to the original rule book, pirates roam the Crowded Sea, close quickly with ships and rush to board them. Fighting them off usually yields treasure from their ship.

pageFacts.text: You begin as a second-level seafaring warrior: lightly equipped, quick on your feet, and already skilled with the scimitar.
Combat is real time. The three action circles appear in dangerous areas and show which sword swings are currently available.
Your scimitar strikes in the direction you face. Press Alt to lock that direction in a corridor; unlock when surrounded.
pageFacts.locator: The combat rhythm, 01 Face the threat

pageFacts.text: Click for the quick attack. Hold the action button longer and release when the second or third circle lights orange.
pageFacts.locator: The combat rhythm, 02 Choose the swing

pageFacts.text: Every blow has a brief readying pause. Land a clean hit, make space, then begin the next attack before closing again.
Ready either the seeking sling or one magic shard. Fire with Space in the direction your Corsair last faced.
pageFacts.locator: The combat rhythm, 04 Switch the left hand

pageFacts.text: Each glowing fragment carries its own remaining charges. One shot spends one charge; when a shard is empty, it breaks apart.
Equip: One shard or the sling. Aim: Face the intended direction. Fire: Press Space.
Zubakon can teach the later swings once experience makes you eligible.
Charge before contact. Do not wait until you are beside a creature to ready the swing.

pageFacts.text: Hit and withdraw. Against powerful foes, secure one blow and back away before the return strike.
